gaps: No documented case study of a faith-app running a genuine small-team, leader-first partnership motion (analogous to the Hallow/YouVersion institution-first model) was found. SmartGroups (closest direct comparable) discloses no growth-tactics data on its own About page. The leader-first alternative is supported only by adjacent, non-faith analogs (EdTech teacher-champion model, Notion Campus Leaders/Ambassador program, general community-led-growth literature) -- genuinely useful as structural analogs per the plan's scope, but not faith-specific precedent, and this must be flagged as hypothesis-not-precedent downstream.

Role-specific pitch-angle literature is asymmetric across the four gatekeeper roles, as the plan anticipated: solid, tactical material exists for small-group leaders (onboarding, engagement, retention) and reasonable material for pastors (though one dedicated pastor-adoption source explicitly does not differentiate pastors from other leaders, which is itself evidence the differentiated literature is thin); diocese/parish-administrator material is real but narrow and skews toward UK Anglican/GDPR compliance documents rather than a US Catholic or general-Protestant-diocese context, and is more about liability/compliance concerns than a persuasive pitch angle; ministry-coordinator-specific pitch literature is the thinnest of the four -- searches surfaced the role's general responsibilities but no dedicated coordinator-targeted outreach/pitch guidance distinct from generic 'church leadership' content.

EveryCampus's own campus-launch materials (its public strategy and launch-guide pages) confirm the coalition/relational emphasis already known from the prior task but do not publicly document chapter-by-chapter rollout mechanics, staffing ratios, or a small-team-scale version of their model -- the deeper operational guide sits behind a gated community platform this round could not access. Whether a single-team, non-coalition version of campus-ministry outreach is feasible remains a reasoned inference from adjacent (non-campus-ministry) ambassador-program literature, not a directly sourced answer.
summary: Round 1 confirmed the prior task's brief.md/conclusion.md as required background (read directly, not re-derived) and then gathered external sources targeting this task's two open questions. Found: (1) a well-corroborated, non-faith-specific 'leader-first vs. institution-first' analog in EdTech go-to-market literature (teacher-first bottom-up adoption, champion-enablement kits, Reach Capital/Agile Education Marketing/EdSurge), reinforced by Notion's Campus Leaders/Ambassador program and general community-led-growth heuristics (early-champion seeding, first-20-50-members-set-culture) as adjacent leader-first precedents; (2) concrete, well-corroborated small-group-leader outreach/onboarding/retention tactics (Text In Church's role-differentiated pitch templates, ChurchTechToday's hands-on-onboarding and check-in cadence, Tabernacle.app's institutional 9-step rollout sequence, free-tier/pilot-as-foot-in-the-door patterns corroborated across SmartGroups and Planning Center); (3) campus-ministry material beyond the single 'relational beats digital' caution, via EveryCampus's own strategy/launch pages (confirming relational emphasis but revealing this operates as a 40+-org coalition, not a small-team playbook) and general campus-ambassador-program literature (Future.com, semester-timing, single-campus-lead delegation model) as a transferability hypothesis; and (4) diocese/parish-administrator-level compliance/liability concerns as a real (though UK-context) documented gatekeeper evaluation dimension distinct from pastor/leader-level pitching. Coverage is asymmetric across the four gatekeeper roles as the plan anticipated, and no faith-specific leader-first precedent exists to directly answer the Hallow/YouVersion transfer question -- both are reported forward as gaps rather than papered over. No debunked prior-task figures (83% referral trust, 30% Catholic-partnership increase, Feb 2024 spike-as-calendar-timing-proof) were re-cited.
